title: Shimon son of Hillel the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman records no halakhah, aggadah, or ordinance of his, and knows his name only from what they said (Shabbat 15a): Hillel, Shimon, Gamliel, and Shimon exercised their patriarchate (nesiut) while the Temple stood, for one hundred years.

Hyman takes it as clearly known that Hillel was nasi for forty years, and concludes that he died, accordingly, sixty years before the destruction, and then his son Shimon was elevated to the patriarchate. It appears that he did not hold office long, not because he died young, but because his father Hillel lived long, so that when his son Shimon rose to the patriarchate he was already very old; and in his seat sat his son, Rabban Gamliel the Elder.

notes.text: Hyman attributes the short patriarchate to Shimon’s advanced age when he inherited office, not to his dying young. “The Elder” qualifies Hillel in the heading.

The consulted Shabbat 15a lists Hillel, Shimon, Gamliel and Shimon and their collective hundred-year patriarchate while the Temple stood. It does not by itself establish Hyman’s forty-year allocation, sixty-year subtraction, exact genealogy or age explanation. Those confident and tentative claims retain Hyman’s respective force, with “the Elder” qualifying Hillel.
